title: Proposed rule would exempt commercial launch licensing from environmental regulations
summary: The Department of Transportation is proposing to exempt commercial space launch licensing from many environmental regulations, which has been welcomed by industry stakeholders but criticized by environmental groups.

title: L3Harris delays missile business IPO to 2027 despite surging defense demand
summary: L3Harris has postponed the IPO of its missile business to 2027, citing market conditions that do not reflect the value of its Pentagon-backed operations. The delay comes despite a surge in defense demand.

title: SpaceX wins $1.6 billion in launch orders for military satellite networks
summary: SpaceX secured $1.6 billion in launch orders for military satellite networks, with Falcon 9 tasked to deploy satellites for missile tracking, targeting, and military communications.

title: Space Force awards All Points $250 million to expand satellite processing at Vandenberg
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded All Points Logistics a $250 million contract to expand satellite processing facilities at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The expansion will enable inspection, testing, fueling, and preparation of satellites for launch vehicle integration.

title: LatConnect 60 Accelerates SWIRSAT Constellation Growth Anchored in Western Australia with Expansion into Malaysia and UAE
summary: LatConnect 60 is expanding its SWIRSAT constellation with operations in Western Australia, Malaysia, and the UAE. The company is focusing on core technology development and payload manufacturing across multiple regions.

title: Fortastra and Hadrian join forces to streamline satellite production
summary: Fortastra, a Los Angeles-based startup focused on space infrastructure defense, is collaborating with Hadrian, a manufacturing specialist, to enhance satellite production using precision machining and additive manufacturing.

title: H3 to launch next ispace lunar lander mission
summary: ispace has chosen Japan's H3 rocket to launch its next lunar lander mission in 2028, marking Japan's first private lunar transportation system.

title: Boeing still working with NASA to schedule next Starliner flight
summary: Boeing is collaborating with NASA to finalize the schedule for the next CST-100 Starliner flight to the International Space Station. The mission will carry cargo as part of the commercial crew program.

title: Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush
summary: A Beijing-based startup raised $14 million to develop a satellite constellation for tracking orbital objects, contributing to China's expanding commercial space situational awareness (SSA) sector.

title: Swift reboost mission encounters attitude control problems
summary: A spacecraft launched to boost NASA's astrophysics satellite's orbit is facing attitude control issues that may threaten its mission. The mission, launched a month ago, aims to reboost the satellite but is now at risk due to these problems.

title: 'It's going to do things that currently are impossible': The Roman Space Telescope, NASA's next great observatory, is ready to launch Aug. 30
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is set to launch on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, promising unprecedented sky mapping capabilities. The mission aims to achieve what is currently impossible in astronomical observation.

title: Watch this stirring new 'Star Trek' 60th anniversary video saluting the iconic sci-fi franchise
summary: Paramount unveiled a tribute video at San Diego Comic-Con celebrating the 60th anniversary of the 'Star Trek' franchise. The video was revealed during a special event marking the iconic sci-fi series' milestone.

title: NASA launched this spacecraft to save a satellite. Now, it needs saving too
summary: NASA's Swift Boost mission was launched to rescue an aging satellite but is now facing control issues itself. The spacecraft's unexpected problems add a new challenge to the mission.

title: SpaceX launching secret US spy satellite early on July 30: Watch it live
summary: SpaceX is set to launch a secret reconnaissance satellite for the U.S. government on July 30, with the event available to watch live. The mission's details remain undisclosed.

title: This genuinely pocket-sized smart telescope makes capturing the deep sky and the solar system almost effortless
summary: A pocket-sized smart telescope has been introduced, making deep sky and solar system observation effortless. The device is designed for accessibility and ease of use.

title: 'The Ark' creator Dean Devlin talks season 3's enormous mystery box and sci-fi surprises (interview)
summary: Dean Devlin discusses the ambitious third season of 'The Ark', revealing it went over budget and became the biggest and craziest season yet. The interview highlights the show's enormous mystery box and sci-fi surprises.

title: The Holy Stone HS900 Pro drone is sadly middling and being outcompeted by many other models
summary: The Holy Stone HS900 Pro drone is considered average and faces strong competition from other models. While it has good features and flight performance, some aspects could be improved with a firmware update.

title: SpaceX Starship still floating 5 days after flight | Space photo of the day for July 29, 2026
summary: SpaceX's Starship remains afloat in the Indian Ocean five days after its latest flight test, with the company continuing to gather imagery of the vehicle. This prolonged floating suggests potential advancements in reusability or recovery operations.

title: On this day in space! July 29, 1982: Soviet Salyut 6 space station falls to Earth
summary: The Soviet Salyut 6 space station re-entered Earth's atmosphere and burned up on July 29, 1982. This marked the end of its operational life after serving as a key platform for long-duration space missions.

title: X-ray spacecraft detects the 36-million-degree 'breath' of an ancient black hole
summary: Astronomers detected the extremely hot emissions from ancient quasars, which are powered by supermassive black holes. The X-ray spacecraft observed these 36-million-degree 'breaths' from the early universe.

title: NASA Awards 2026 Innovative Technology Concepts
summary: NASA's Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program has awarded 18 new grants totaling $3.2 million to support visionary aerospace technology ideas for solar system exploration and universe understanding. Each Phase I award provides up to $175,000 for a nine-month initial study.

title: NASA Sets Coverage for August Northern Hemisphere Total Solar Eclipse
summary: NASA will provide live coverage of a total solar eclipse on August 12, visible in parts of Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, Spain, and Portugal. The event will include expert interviews and multiple streaming platforms.

title: NASA’s Curiosity Views a Sand-Capped Butte
summary: NASA's Curiosity Mars rover captured an image of a sand-capped butte named 'Miraflores' on Mars. The butte, about 20 feet tall, was formed as surrounding rock eroded away over time.

title: NASA’s Curiosity Discovers a Field of Martian Polygons
summary: NASA's Curiosity rover discovered a field of polygonal surface features on Mars, marking the first time so many polygons have been observed in one location. This discovery adds to previous observations of such features by the rover.

title: NASA’s Curiosity Mars Rover Discovers Field of Honeycomb Textures
summary: NASA's Curiosity Mars Rover discovered honeycomb-like polygonal fractures on Mars while climbing 'Valle Grande'. The geometric textures, each about 1.5 to 3 inches across, have been observed multiple times during the mission.

title: APOD: 2026 July 29 – Psyche Receives Gravity Assist from Mars
summary: The Psyche spacecraft received a gravity assist from Mars as part of its mission to explore the asteroid Psyche. This maneuver will help the spacecraft adjust its trajectory toward its destination.

title: Understanding How Martian Auroras Are Made
summary: NASA's MAVEN mission has discovered that certain Martian auroras form similarly to Earth's, with charged particles from solar storms interacting with Mars' atmosphere. The findings help explain atmospheric loss on Mars and were highlighted in a July 23, 2026 illustration.

title: NASA Webb Explores Family Tree of Newly Discovered Distant Objects
summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope discovered little red dots (LRDs) in 2022, which are extremely distant, compact red sources. These objects are theorized to be supermassive black holes, sparking significant astronomical interest.

title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Ray Williams
summary: NASA has converted contractor Ray Williams to a civil servant role at Stennis Space Center, where he now supervises test operations support. This move aligns with NASA's plan to restore core competencies by transitioning contractors to civil service positions.

title: Sizing Up the Sargassum Belt
summary: The Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt reached near-record seaweed levels in June 2026, with the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of America hitting all-time highs.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 showcased Ship 40's successful mission completion and intact return, paving the way for future catch attempts. The flawless flight highlights progress in the vehicle's reliability and operational capabilities.

summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China and a Falcon 9 launch. The launches are part of ongoing global spaceflight activities.

summary: NASA's Juno mission reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geological features.

summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for future missions.

summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship program.

summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing challenges in the Starship program's development.

summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman. The mission aims to demonstrate in-space servicing capabilities.

summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new attempt at the Starship Flight 13 launch after a previous abort. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are scheduled for upcoming launches.

summary: Three companies—Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space—are making progress on their new rocket developments: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5, respectively. This comes as the industry also watches SpaceX's Starship test program.

summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission uses a coronagraph to block the Sun's glare, allowing it to observe the Sun's corona and Earth simultaneously. This technology enables unique scientific observations by playing a 'hide and seek' game with the Sun.

summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with the European space industry. The two-day event at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands aims to exchange ideas and explore opportunities.

summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication and radar systems in the space industry.

summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to the CM25 meeting, outlining planned activities and industrial opportunities. These events aim to facilitate direct exchange between ESA and industry stakeholders.

summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and its ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

summary: Outlier Space secured $7.35M to develop New Zealand's first reentry vehicle for microgravity research, with its first mission planned for 2028.

title: ESA taps Aalyria to build deep-space network hub
summary: ESA has selected Aalyria to construct a network-operations center for deep-space communication, enabling reliable data sharing across the solar system. This initiative aims to enhance interplanetary connectivity for spacecraft.

summary: A new report outlines potential future trajectories for Africa's space industry as the continent aims to establish itself as a significant player in the global space sector. The analysis highlights strategic opportunities and challenges for Africa's growing space ecosystem.

summary: ORBES introduced the Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft, a 12U, sub-26-kg satellite designed for inspection missions and deployable via customer infrastructure. The spacecraft aims to provide ready-to-go maintenance services in orbit.

summary: Impulse Space has unveiled its first electric propulsion system, named Electra, designed for long-duration space operations. The announcement follows a year of exploration into developing such technology.

title: Skywave to Add Iridium SBS Data Service Into Industrial IoT Offering
summary: Skywave, a company under Iridium and Orbcomm, has partnered with Iridium to integrate its Short Burst Data (SBD) services into its industrial IoT offerings for heavy equipment OEM customers. This marks the first collaboration of its kind.

title: Virgin Media O2 Exec Explains Strategic Approach to Direct-to-Device With O2 Satellite
summary: Virgin Media O2, a major U.K. mobile operator, has launched O2 Satellite, a direct-to-device service enabled by satellite technology. An executive explains the company's strategic approach to this new offering.

title: Space-Based Data Centers: Inside the Race to Move Compute to Orbit
summary: The space industry is exploring the concept of space-based data centers to meet the growing demand for computing power driven by AI, with recent developments highlighting increased interest in moving infrastructure to orbit.
